title_en: 278: How to Build a Balanced Portfolio and Navigate Market Volatility: Your investing questions answered
title_zh: 278｜如何构建均衡组合、应对市场波动：听众投资问答特辑（主持 Oscar Pulido 对话 BlackRock 的 Kristy Akullian）
subtitle_zh: BlackRock 的 Kristy Akullian 回答听众提问：投资如何起步、债券与期货机制，以及如何在 AI 热潮中甄别真机会。
summary_zh: 本期 The Bid 是一集有问必答（Ask Me Anything）特辑，主持 Oscar Pulido 把话筒交给听众，请来 BlackRock 美洲区 Global Portfolio Solutions 投资策略主管 Kristy Akullian 逐题回答。爱丁堡 22 岁的 Yash 问该如何起步，Akullian 强调两件事：尽早开始，并给你的钱分配不同的工作——为退休、也为买车买房这类中短期目标分别投资，不同期限对应不同风险水平。30 岁的 Andrea 问如何衡量进展，她抛出能被衡量的东西才能被管理好（what gets measured gets managed），建议建立财务卫生（financial hygiene）习惯：设预算、定投入金额、随收入把数字往上提，并重视税前投资（pre-tax investments）的复利空间。面对 Sergio 关于长期持有与短期反应如何平衡的提问，她引用数据：过去 20 年市场表现最好的 25 个交易日中，有 24 天出现在最差交易日前后一个月之内——市场处理新信息时常常过度反应，择时（timing the market）反而最容易犯错。节目后半进入产品机制：她解释债券是组合中的压舱物（ballast）与分散化工具（diversifier），以及利率与债券价格的反向关系；解释期货是衍生品合约（derivatives contract）与零和游戏（zero sum game），从 S&P 500 期货、石油期货到猪腩（pork belly）期货，都可对标的资产未来价格下注或对冲。谈到 AI，她观察到分化从硬件跑赢软件进入更细阶段——投资者关注谁在开支票（writing the checks）、谁在兑支票（cashing the checks），因此在全球不同行业看到显著的市场表现分散（dispersion）。对资本开支（CAPEX）会不会挤出其他行业投资的疑问，她判断这不一定是全面挤出，但抬高了投资门槛与回报率，加剧了组合集中度。她送投资者一句话：不要在选择市场时机上自作聪明，停留在市场里的时间远比买卖某个主题的具体时点更重要。是一堂把入门、机制与主题打通的问答课。
description: 278: How to Build a Balanced Portfolio and Navigate Market Volatility: Your investing questions answered

turns.en: Investing can raise a lot of questions, whether you're just getting started or have been investing for years. How do you know if you're on track financially? How do you separate a good AI investment from the hype? And what's the biggest mistake even experience investors make?
turns.zh: 投资会引出一大堆问题，无论你是刚开始入门，还是已经投了很多年。你怎么知道自己的财务状况是不是走在正轨上？怎么把真正好的 AI 投资和单纯的炒作区分开来？还有，连经验丰富的投资者都会犯的最大错误是什么？

turns.en: Welcome to the big, where we break down what's happening in the markets and explore the forces changing the economy and finance. I'm Oscar Polito. Today, we're doing something a little different. We're handing the microphone over to you, our listeners, for another Ask Me Anything episode.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 The Bid，在这档节目里，我们会拆解市场上正在发生的事情，探讨那些正在改变经济和金融的力量。我是 Oscar Pulido。今天我们要做点不太一样的事情：我们要把麦克风交给你们——我们的听众，这是又一期的「有问必答」（Ask Me Anything）特辑。

turns.en: To help me answer them, I'm joined by Kristi Akulian, head of Global Portfolio Solutions Investment Strategy for the Americas. We'll discuss your general investing questions from how to start building wealth and navigating market volatility to understanding bonds, futures, and the opportunities and risks surrounding AI.
turns.zh: 为了帮我回答这些问题，我今天请来了 Kristy Akullian，她担任美洲区 Global Portfolio Solutions 的投资策略主管。我们会聊聊大家提出的各种投资问题，从如何开始积累财富、如何应对市场波动，到理解债券、期货，以及围绕 AI 的机会与风险。

turns.en: Kristi, thank you so much for joining us on the bid. Thank you so much for having me. It's been a long time, Gold. Well, this is your first time on the podcast. We appreciate you joining us. We're putting you in an interesting spot. This is one of our Ask Me Anything episodes where we've gone out to our listeners and we've
turns.zh: Kristy，非常感谢你来 The Bid 做客。非常感谢你们的邀请。感觉我们已经认识很久了。嗯，其实这是你第一次上我们的播客，很感谢你能来。我们把你放在了一个挺有意思的位置上：这是我们的「有问必答」特辑之一，我们去向听众征集了问题，然后

turns.en: asked them to send in their questions just about general investment trends or questions that they have and we're asking you to answer them. So we're going to start with a question that I think will resonate with a lot of our listeners, particularly those who are just beginning their investing journey.
turns.zh: 请他们把自己关于整体投资趋势的疑问、或者心里想问的问题发过来，再请你来回答。所以我们先从一个问题开始，我觉得这个问题会引起很多听众的共鸣，尤其是那些刚刚开始投资之旅的人。

turns.en: And our first question is going to come from Yash in Edinburgh. Hi, my name is Yash, I'm 22 years old, I'm from Edinburgh. One of the things I wanted to know is just in the global markets these days, everything's changing all the time. There's new stuff coming about.
turns.zh: 第一个问题来自爱丁堡的 Yash。「大家好，我叫 Yash，今年 22 岁，来自爱丁堡。我想知道的是，如今全球市场随时都在变化，不断有新东西冒出来。」

turns.en: So there's a young person myself looking to start getting into investing, what's the best approach forward and how can I consistently compound my money that can help me for the future but also help me know? So Christy, what would you say to Yash? Perfect. So my first time here and it's really a trial by fire, right? It asked me anything.
turns.zh: 「所以，作为一个想要开始踏入投资领域的年轻人，接下来最好的做法是什么？我要怎么让自己的钱持续复利滚起来，既对将来有帮助，也对当下有帮助？」那么 Kristy，你会怎么回答 Yash？太好了，我这第一次上节目，简直就是直接被扔进火里接受考验，对吧，还是「有问必答」。

turns.en: This is a perfect place to start. I think as investors are really thinking about investing, the most important thing you can do is start early and I would also say give your money different jobs. So many of us here from financial professionals and we get the advice to start investing for your retirement right away.
turns.zh: 这真是一个绝佳的切入点。我觉得投资者在真正思考投资这件事时，最重要的一点就是尽早开始；另外我还想说，要给你的钱分配不同的「工作」。我们很多人都是从金融专业人士那里听到这样的建议：马上开始为退休做投资。

turns.en: If you're 22, that can feel so far away. I'd also like to encourage people to start thinking and investing towards near term goals as well. Near and medium terms. Do you want to buy a car in the future? Do you want to buy a house in the future? Those are going to be investments that have different levels of risk than what you should
turns.zh: 但如果你才 22 岁，退休会感觉遥不可及。所以我也想鼓励大家开始为近期目标去思考和投资，包括近期和中期的目标。你将来想买车吗？想买房吗？这些目标对应的投资，其风险水平和你现在应该承担的

turns.en: be taking now if you're 22 and you're thinking about retiring in 40 plus years. So start early and have a plan and have a different plan for different goals. I like that. Give your money different jobs, which I think is what you're saying is that you're going
turns.zh: 风险是不一样的——如果你 22 岁，想的是 40 多年以后退休的话。所以要尽早开始，要有计划，而且要为不同的目标制定不同的计划。我喜欢这个说法：「给你的钱分配不同的工作」。我理解你的意思是，你

turns.en: to have different goals over different time horizons and therefore can invest along those different time horizons. Getting started early, of course, is important, but everyone's financial situation is going to be different. And that brings us to our next question from Andrea, who's wondering how to measure financial
turns.zh: 会在不同的时间跨度上有着不同的目标，因此也可以按照这些不同的时间跨度去投资。当然，尽早开始很重要，但每个人的财务状况都不一样。这就引出了我们的下一个问题，来自 Andrea，她想知道该如何衡量自己的财务

turns.en: progress when we're all at different stages of life. Hi, I'm Andrea. I'm 30 years old. I hear a lot of people talking about investing and building their portfolio at my age, but we're all just at different stages of life. So I'm curious, how do I know if I'm doing well financially at my age and what should
turns.zh: 进展，毕竟我们都处在人生的不同阶段。「大家好，我是 Andrea，今年 30 岁。我经常听到很多人在谈论我这个年纪该怎么投资、怎么搭建自己的投资组合，但我们都处在人生的不同阶段。所以我很好奇，我怎么才能知道自己在这个年纪的财务状况算不算好？在 30 多岁时投资，我应该

turns.en: I be prioritizing when it comes to investing in my 30s? That's a great question. And as we get a little bit older, I think that we start to consider different financial needs as well. It's certainly important that we prioritize those long term retirement goals, pre-tax investments
turns.zh: 把什么放在优先考虑的位置？」这是个很好的问题。随着我们年纪稍长，我觉得我们会开始考虑不同的财务需求。当然，把长期的退休目标放在优先位置很重要，税前投资（pre-tax investments）

turns.en: are so valuable, especially at this age, because we have so much time to compound them. But again, at your 30s, this is critical point where you probably have a little bit more discretionary money after you paid the bills than you did in your 20s. I like to say that what gets measured gets managed.
turns.zh: 尤其宝贵，特别是在这个年纪，因为我们有足够长的时间让它复利增长。但同样，30 多岁是一个关键节点：付完账单之后，你可以自由支配的钱大概会比 20 多岁时多一些。我喜欢说一句话：能被衡量的东西，才能被管理好（what gets measured gets managed）。

turns.en: So it's really important to build in some financial hygiene right now, to set budgets, set goals about how much you want to invest and see how you can grow that with your income over time. So yes, absolutely focus on retirement, but now is also that time to start building that
turns.zh: 所以，现在就开始建立一些良好的财务习惯（financial hygiene）真的很重要：设定预算，设定你想投入多少钱的目标，然后看看随着收入增长，你能怎么把这个数字往上提。所以，没错，一定要关注退休，但现在也正是开始培养那种

turns.en: muscle memory about setting some money aside every month to maybe do after tax investing, to be able to put some money aside for some of those shorter term goals that are going to be here before retirement. You have a way of coming up with really memorable one line or so you mentioned what gets
turns.zh: 「肌肉记忆」的时候——每个月留出一笔钱，也许用于税后投资（after-tax investing），为那些在退休之前就会到来的较短期的目标存下一些钱。你真的很擅长想出这种让人印象深刻的一句话，比如你刚才提到的「能被衡量的

turns.en: measured gets managed and I think here what you're alluding to is maybe just showing a little bit more discipline as you start to go from that very early part of your financial journey into slightly later stage of your financial journey. Now, having a long term investment plan is one thing, but sticking to it can be another,
turns.zh: 东西才能被管理好」。我觉得你在这里暗示的，也许就是在你的财务旅程从最早期走向稍后阶段时，要多表现出一点自律。有一个长期的投资计划是一回事，但能不能坚持执行又是另一回事，

turns.en: especially when markets are moving around, which we've definitely seen very recently. Sergio has a question about something I suspect even the most experienced investor struggle with. Hi, this is Sergio Lez. Investors are constantly being told to think long term.
turns.zh: 尤其是在市场上下震荡的时候——这一点我们最近可是看得清清楚楚。Sergio 的问题涉及一个我猜连最有经验的投资者都会纠结的事情。「大家好，我是 Sergio Lez。投资者总是被告知要着眼长期。」

turns.en: So how do you balance that advice with the temptation to react to what's happening in the markets today? Yeah, and so much is happening in markets today. Let's just start by acknowledging that. I think we are in a more volatile, more concentrated period for markets. And so there is even more of a temptation to react to that.
turns.zh: 「那么，你该如何在这样的建议，与想要对当下市场变化做出反应的诱惑之间取得平衡？」是啊，现在的市场正在发生太多事情，我们得先承认这一点。我觉得市场正处在一个波动更大、集中度更高的时期，所以想要对此做出反应的诱惑也就更大。

turns.en: I think it's really important to remember that over the last 20 years, 24 out of 25 of the best ever days in the market came within one month of the worst ever day in the market. So markets tend to overreact to news as they're processing and digesting new pieces of information. And typically we'll see some really sharp selloffs.
turns.zh: 我觉得有一点非常重要，一定要记住：在过去 20 年里，市场表现最好的 25 个交易日当中，有 24 天都出现在市场表现最差的那些交易日前后一个月之内。市场在处理和消化新信息的过程中往往会过度反应，所以我们通常会看到一些非常剧烈的抛售。

turns.en: And sometimes those are followed by really sharp rebounds. So we as investors need to be a little bit emotionally disciplined about not overreacting as well. So we can't get out of the market at the worst time. I think it's really important just to say and because if you do, you may miss that bounce on the other side.
turns.zh: 而有时候，剧烈抛售之后紧跟着的就是非常强劲的反弹。所以我们作为投资者，在情绪上也要有一点自律，不要自己也过度反应，不要在最糟糕的时刻退出市场。我觉得这一点必须说清楚，因为如果你真的那么做了，你可能会错过另一头的反弹。

turns.en: And then before thinking even a little bit long term, just out of some of those day-to-day moves, investors also have to be comfortable with a little bit of volatility because without risk, there's no reward. So even though markets, if we look at the S&P 500 as an example, tend to be up about
turns.zh: 另外，哪怕只是从日常的波动来看、还没说到长期，投资者也必须能接受一定的波动性，因为没有风险就没有回报（without risk, there's no reward）。以 S&P 500 为例，尽管市场大约有

turns.en: 75% of the time and on average, they're up about 9%. Almost every year, we still see about a 14% drawdown. So it's markets don't just go up into the right. We have to be comfortable with that volatility because it's that risk that brings the reward with it. Right.
turns.zh: 75% 的时间是上涨的，平均涨幅约为 9%，但几乎每一年我们仍然会看到大约 14% 的回撤（drawdown）。所以市场并不是一路只涨不跌、直线向上的。我们必须能接受这种波动，因为正是那份风险带来了回报。没错。

turns.en: And Christie, you and I have been doing this for a while and we know that investing is a full contact sport. While it can be very rewarding over the long term, it can be a very emotional rollercoaster. And what you're saying is those people who can control their emotions are probably going to have a little bit more success.
turns.zh: Kristy，你和我做这行都有一段时间了，我们知道投资是一项「全接触式」的运动。长期来看它可能回报丰厚，但过程也可能是一趟情绪过山车。你的意思是，那些能够控制自己情绪的人，大概会更容易成功一些。

turns.en: Let's turn to some of the building blocks of investing. We've talked a lot about stocks, but bonds can also play a very important role in a portfolio. And with interest rates being such an important driver of markets, understanding how they affect bonds can be confusing. Here's Biotta with our next question. My name is Biotta.
turns.zh: 我们来说说投资的一些基本构件。我们已经谈了很多股票，但债券在一个投资组合里也能扮演非常重要的角色。而利率又是市场如此重要的驱动因素，理解利率如何影响债券可能会让人一头雾水。下一个问题来自 Biotta。「我叫 Biotta。」

turns.en: I'm 28 years old and my question today is around fixed income, in particular, how do changes in interest rates affect bond prices and yields? And why might bonds with different maturity's durations and credit quality respond differently to the same changes in the market interest rates? That is an excellent question.
turns.zh: 「我今年 28 岁，今天想问的是关于固定收益（fixed income）的问题，具体来说，利率的变化会如何影响债券价格和收益率？为什么期限、久期（duration）和信用质量不同的债券，对市场利率同样变化的反应会不一样？」这是个非常好的问题。

turns.en: And not one that I would say most people know to ask at 28. So congratulations to Biotta for that one. Yeah, I think that a lot of people have looked at bonds as a necessary evil in their portfolio where they have felt like maybe they weren't giving them much in terms of returns.
turns.zh: 而且我得说，这不是大多数人在 28 岁时会想到要问的问题，所以 Biotta 这个问题问得漂亮。是啊，我觉得很多人一直把债券看作组合里的「必要之恶」（necessary evil），感觉债券在回报上给不了他们太多东西。

turns.en: But it's important to remember that a balanced portfolio doesn't all move together. And so bonds can serve as a really important source of ballast in a portfolio which it doesn't seem as important when equity markets are just going up. But it's certainly when we see those periods of volatility and where some of the more
turns.zh: 但很重要的一点是要记住，一个均衡的投资组合并不是所有部分都同涨同跌的。债券可以充当组合里非常重要的「压舱物」（ballast）——在股票市场一路向上的时候，它看起来没那么重要；但当我们经历那些波动时期，当一些比较

turns.en: popular trades like we have seen so far this year come under pressure. The specifics of bond mechanics as Biotta noted, when interest rates grow up, bond prices go down. Bond prices are going to be sensitive to interest rates because conceptually if you own a bond
turns.zh: 热门的交易（就像我们今年迄今看到的那些）开始承压时，它的作用就凸显出来了。说到债券机制的具体细节，正如 Biotta 提到的：利率上行时，债券价格下跌。债券价格之所以对利率敏感，是因为从概念上讲，如果你持有一只

turns.en: that is at a 4% interest rate, for example, an interest rates move up to 5%. The new bonds that are being issued now are going to be that much more attractive. So your bond's price is going to fall as a result. Duration you can think of is just a measure of interest rate sensitivity.
turns.zh: 利率为 4% 的债券，而利率升到了 5%，那么现在新发行的债券就会因此更有吸引力，所以你手上那只债券的价格就会随之下跌。久期（duration）你可以把它理解成对利率敏感度的一个衡量指标，

turns.en: How sensitive is your bond to change as an interest rate? So longer duration bonds which tend to have a longer maturity as well are going to see bigger price swings from even the same kind of percentage change in interest rates. And then the last part of that too is credit.
turns.zh: 也就是你的债券对利率变化有多敏感。所以久期更长的债券——它们往往到期期限也更长——即便面对同样幅度的利率变动，价格波动也会更大。最后还有一个部分，就是信用（credit）。

turns.en: Just like all of us have a credit score, bonds are going to trade at a level that reflects the ability of the issuer to pay that back. And so as companies are stronger with healthier earnings and stronger balance sheets, they will have narrower spreads, a higher credit quality. And then of course that happens in reverse too.
turns.zh: 就像我们每个人都有一个信用评分一样，债券的交易价格水平会反映发行人的偿债能力。所以当公司更强、盈利更健康、资产负债表更稳健时，它们的利差（spreads）会更窄，信用质量更高。当然，反过来也是一样的。

turns.en: So bonds are always reacting and responding to both changes in interest rates, which is a little more universal and changes in the corporate structure or specific company news as well. And I agree with you. I think most people in their 20s aren't maybe thinking about bonds in the sort of detail that Beatta is thinking about it.
turns.zh: 所以债券始终在对两方面的变化做出反应：一是利率变化，这更具普遍性；二是公司结构的变化或者特定公司的新闻。我同意你的看法。我想大多数 20 多岁的人，可能不会像 Biotta 那样细致地去思考债券。

turns.en: But as you've outlined, they play an important role of ballast in a portfolio and can be a good diversifier to the stock market, which is often what we find ourselves talking about. So we've talked about bonds. There are plenty of other investment tools that people hear.
turns.zh: 但正如你梳理的那样，债券在组合中扮演着重要的「压舱物」角色，可以是股票市场很好的分散化工具（diversifier）——而这正是我们经常谈论的东西。好了，我们聊完了债券。还有很多别的投资工具是人们经常

turns.en: There are plenty of other investment tools that people hear about without necessarily knowing how they work. Christie, if you think Beatta was a student of the market talking about bonds, this one is really going to impress you. This next question is about futures.
turns.zh: 听到、却不一定知道它们是怎么运作的。Kristy，如果你觉得 Biotta 谈债券时已经算是个认真钻研市场的人，那么下一个问题真的会让你印象深刻——这个问题是关于期货（futures）的。

turns.en: Bridget has a question about what they actually are and why investors use them. Hi, my name is Bridget Utacoya and one question I've been hoping somebody would explain to me is, what are futures? When would you use them and why? I love this question. I spent a lot of my career focusing on equity derivatives.
turns.zh: Bridget 想问期货究竟是什么、投资者为什么要用它们。「大家好，我叫 Bridget Utacoya，我一直希望有人能给我解释的一个问题是：什么是期货？什么时候会用到它们？为什么要用？」我太喜欢这个问题了。我职业生涯中很大一部分时间都在研究股票衍生品（equity derivatives）。

turns.en: So it warms my heart that anybody cares, especially young people. But yeah, futures go back very far. These are one of the oldest financial instruments in the world. They were originally used as a way for farmers and agriculture producers to be able to hedge their crops in the future.
turns.zh: 所以看到有人关心这个话题，我心里很暖，尤其是年轻人。是啊，期货的历史非常久远，它们是世界上最早的金融工具之一。最初，期货是农民和农产品生产商用来对未来的收成进行对冲（hedge）的一种方式。

turns.en: At the foundation level, futures are a derivatives contract and that means that they are a zero sum game. So somebody has to go long for every short and vice versa. And what they are is just a way to set on or hedge against future price movements in the underlying. So there's futures across all different types of financial assets.
turns.zh: 从本质上讲，期货是一种衍生品合约（derivatives contract），这意味着它是一个零和游戏（zero sum game）：每一笔空头都必须对应一个做多的人，反之亦然。它的作用就是让你对标的资产未来的价格走势下注或者进行对冲。所以各种类型的金融资产都有对应的期货。

turns.en: There's futures on the S&P 500. There's futures on oil. There's futures on pork belly contracts. You could really get as specific as you want. But what they do is let you get exposure to movements in the underlying without necessarily needing to put up the cash to go by the underlying.
turns.zh: 有 S&P 500 期货，有石油期货，还有猪腩（pork belly）期货，你真的可以想多具体就多具体。而它们的作用，是让你获得对标的资产价格变动的敞口（exposure），却不一定需要真的拿出现金去买下那个标的。

turns.en: So for a financial future, for example, in the S&P 500, you can get exposure to whatever the movements are in the underlying index over the next three months or six months or nine months if you continue to roll that contract without needing to have the cash to go by those underlying stocks.
turns.zh: 所以，拿金融期货举例，比如 S&P 500 期货，你可以获得对未来三个月、六个月或九个月里标的指数涨跌的敞口——只要你持续展期（roll）这份合约——而不需要手里有现金去买下那些成分股。

turns.en: So what that means is that futures provide leverage. And I know a lot of investors, there's a lot of questions about leverage right now and what that means, whether it's in levered products and levered ETFs, we've certainly seen rise. But yes, futures are used for leverage on the long side.
turns.zh: 这就意味着期货提供了杠杆（leverage）。我知道很多投资者现在对杠杆、以及杠杆意味着什么有很多疑问，不管是杠杆产品还是杠杆 ETF（levered ETFs），我们都确实看到它们在增多。是的，期货可以被用来在多头一侧加杠杆。

turns.en: But really, I think it's important to remember that they're also used as a hedging instrument for many types of investors, whether that is farmers hedging their crops, whether that is airlines hedging the price of oil prices. It just gives you more certainty today about what price you're going to have to pay tomorrow. Right.
turns.zh: 但我觉得更重要的是要记住，期货对很多类型的投资者来说也是一种对冲工具，不管是农民对冲他们的农作物，还是航空公司对冲油价。它只是让你今天就能更确定明天要付的价格是多少。没错。

turns.en: And futures, as you mentioned, are derivatives. We're getting into some more technical areas. And like you mentioned, not just individual investors who could use them to express a view, but you mentioned in the agricultural sector or airlines in the industrial sector that are using it as a way to manage risk in their businesses.
turns.zh: 正如你提到的，期货是衍生品，我们正在进入一些更技术性的领域。而且就像你说的，不只是个人投资者可以用它来表达自己的观点，你还提到农业领域、或者工业领域里的航空公司，都在用期货作为管理自身业务风险的一种方式。

turns.en: Christy, we weren't going to leave this conversation without a question about artificial intelligence. AI has attracted enormous attention and investment, as you know, but not every company associated with the technology will necessarily be a winner. So here's Alex and London who wants to know how investors can separate the opportunities
turns.zh: Kristy，我们这场对话不可能不聊人工智能（AI）就结束。如你所知，AI 已经吸引了大量的关注和投资，但并不是每一家与这项技术相关的公司最终都会成为赢家。下面这个问题来自伦敦的 Alex，他想知道投资者该如何把机会

turns.en: from the hype. Hi, I'm Alex from London. How can an investor differentiate between a value AI stock or an AI company that's simply riding the wave and more ultimately proved to be a poor investment? It's an excellent question, especially because the history of the AI trade has evolved very quickly.
turns.zh: 和炒作区分开来。「大家好，我是来自伦敦的 Alex。投资者该如何区分一只真正有价值的 AI 股票，和一家只是随波逐流、最终被证明是糟糕投资的 AI 公司？」这是个很好的问题，尤其是因为 AI 交易这段历史的演进速度非常快。

turns.en: If we look at 24 and 25, it feels like almost anything that was AI or AI, Jason was moving up and everything was sort of riding that wave. I think 2026 this year, so far, we've seen a real differentiation in terms of how investors are treating different parts of the AI stack.
turns.zh: 如果我们看 24 年和 25 年，感觉几乎所有跟 AI 沾边或者与 AI 相关（AI-adjacent）的东西都在上涨，全都算是在乘着那一波浪。而我觉得 2026 年，也就是今年到目前为止，我们已经看到投资者在对待 AI 技术栈（AI stack）的不同部分时，出现了真正的分化。

turns.en: I think earlier this year, the first hint that we got of that was this very large discrepancy between the performance of software and the performance of hardware and hardware, obviously being necessary to the build out of AI, whereas software came under pressure as potentially being replaced by it.
turns.zh: 我觉得今年早些时候，我们得到的第一个迹象，就是软件的表现和硬件的表现之间出现了非常大的反差——硬件显然是 AI 建设（build out）所必需的，而软件则因为可能被 AI 取代而承压。

turns.en: That was phase one, maybe, of this differentiation. As we moved over the course of the year, I think investors have increasingly been paying attention to who's riding the checks and who's caching the checks. What are the companies that are responsible for the AI build out?
turns.zh: 那也许就是这轮分化的第一阶段。随着今年时间的推进，我觉得投资者越来越关注谁在开支票（writing the checks）、谁在兑支票（cashing the checks），也就是哪些公司要为 AI 的建设投入买单？

turns.en: This can be some of the hyperscalers, some of those biggest companies that we know that make up the biggest portion of the indices as well versus maybe some of the memory chip companies, some of the semiconductors that are needed to build out. Then more recently, I think where we are now in terms of this to answer the question and
turns.zh: 这里面可能有一些超大规模云服务商（hyperscalers），也就是我们都知道的、在指数中占比最大的那些公司；而另一边，可能是内存芯片公司，以及建设 AI 所需要的一些半导体公司。再往后，也就是我觉得我们现在所处的阶段——为了回答这个问题，

turns.en: get a little more specific in terms of how investors are finding value in the AI chain, it's really about what companies can do well and higher interest rates. That's the flush out that we're seeing here a little bit. Where higher quality AI companies are being rewarded right now, the ones with stronger
turns.zh: 并且更具体地说说投资者是如何在 AI 链条中发现价值的：关键其实在于哪些公司能在更高的利率环境下表现得好。这就是我们现在看到的一定程度的「洗牌」（flush out）：更高质量的 AI 公司眼下正在得到奖励，也就是那些

turns.en: balance sheets and stronger earnings, where some of the lower quality, more speculative parts of the AI market have really been punished recently. That speaks to market volatility, and I think what you're saying is that investors are becoming a bit more discerning about where they invest along this AI theme and therefore
turns.zh: 资产负债表更稳健、盈利更强的公司；而 AI 市场中一些质量较低、更具投机性的部分，最近真的受到了惩罚。这说的就是市场波动性。我觉得你的意思是，投资者在沿着 AI 这条主题投资时，正在变得更有鉴别力，因此

turns.en: why we're seeing some dispersion in the marketplace across many different sectors and regions of the world. We're going to stick with AI. We've seen companies committing significant amounts of money to building the infrastructure and technology behind it. You mentioned the CAPEX, but what does that mean for the rest of the economy?
turns.zh: 我们才会在全球许多不同的行业和地区看到市场表现的分散（dispersion）。我们继续聊 AI。我们已经看到各家公司投入大量资金去建设 AI 背后的基础设施和技术。你提到了资本开支（CAPEX），那么这对经济的其他部分意味着什么？

turns.en: ANZ has a question about whether all that investment in AI could be coming at the expense of other sectors. Hi, my name is Mackenzie. To what extent do you think AI is crowding out spending from other sectors of the economy? And what impacts could this have for economies in the future?
turns.zh: ANZ 的问题是关于这些投向 AI 的巨额资金，会不会是以牺牲其他行业为代价。「大家好，我叫 Mackenzie。你觉得 AI 在多大程度上正在挤占（crowding out）经济中其他行业的支出？这未来会对各经济体产生什么影响？」

turns.en: Yeah, I think that when we go and talk to investors right now, increasingly the conversation isn't just, how do I get exposure to AI? What are the knock on impacts of having so much AI in my portfolio and in the economy more broadly? I do think that there is an element of truth to this. There is certainly a competition for capital.
turns.zh: 是的。我觉得我们现在去和投资者交流时，话题已经不只是「我怎么才能获得 AI 的敞口」，而是「我的组合里有这么多 AI，以及在更广泛的经济中有这么多 AI，会带来哪些连带影响（knock-on impacts）」。我确实认为这个说法有几分道理：资本的竞争肯定是存在的。

turns.en: Money is fungible, and if it gets all funneled into one place, it's not going to somewhere else by definition, right? So I do think that we've seen the reflection of some of that competition for capital is that we've seen yields rise as more investors are trying to fund some of that AI build out.
turns.zh: 钱是可替代的（fungible），如果它全都被导流到一个地方，那么按定义它就不会流到别的地方去，对吧？所以我确实认为，我们看到了一些这种资本竞争的反映：随着越来越多投资者试图为 AI 建设融资，收益率在上行。

turns.en: It's pushing up the cost of capital for other industries as well. It doesn't necessarily signal to me that we are crowding out all other investments. But what it does signal to me is that there is a higher bar and a higher required rate of return on investment required right now.
turns.zh: 这也在推高其他行业的资本成本。对我来说，这并不一定意味着我们正在挤出所有其他投资；但它确实向我表明，如今投资的门槛更高了，所要求的投资回报率也更高了。

turns.en: And it also means really importantly for investors that portfolios are getting more concentrated. And there's more need to seek outside sources of diversification that may be away from some of this AI spending as well. And in fact, we recently talked to Kerry King and Alex Brazier about just the interesting
turns.zh: 而且对投资者来说，非常重要的一点是，投资组合正在变得更加集中，因此更需要去寻找组合之外的分散化来源，也许是与这些 AI 支出保持距离的领域。事实上，我们最近和 Carrie King 以及 Alex Brazier 聊过这个很有意思的

turns.en: exercise of diversifying beyond this AI theme. And they talked about things like the healthcare sector and maybe market neutral strategies. But I'm sure Christie, if we had more time, you'd probably tell us there's an even longer list to have to evaluate. We've taken quite a tour.
turns.zh: 话题：如何在 AI 主题之外做分散化。他们谈到了医疗保健行业，也许还有市场中性策略（market neutral strategies）。不过 Kristy，我相信如果时间再多一点，你大概会告诉我们，需要评估的清单还要更长。我们今天绕了一大圈。

turns.en: We've talked about the basics of getting started with investing. We've talked about bonds futures. We've talked about the AI theme. But I want to take us back to a question now that is really about the fundamentals because no matter how much experience you have, there's always something to learn. So here's Natika with our final question.
turns.zh: 我们聊了开始投资的基础知识，聊了债券和期货，也聊了 AI 主题。但现在我想把我们带回一个真正关乎根本的问题，因为无论你有多少经验，总还是有东西可以学。最后一个问题来自 Natika。

turns.en: What's one thing about investing that you think even experienced investors get wrong? I think one of the most important challenges that investors face is just trying not to get too cute with timing the market. When we look at the totality of investment returns over time, we find that what you can
turns.zh: 「你觉得关于投资，有哪一件事是连经验丰富的投资者都会搞错的？」我觉得投资者面临的最重要挑战之一，就是不要在选择市场时机（timing the market）这件事上自作聪明。当我们审视长时间里投资回报的整体情况时，会发现

turns.en: spend in terms of how much time in the market is so much more important than whether you got the exact day right in terms of trading in or out of a certain theme. And I think that's great insight. Timing the market is very difficult, no matter what your level of experience is.
turns.zh: 你在市场中停留的时间有多长，远比你在买入或卖出某个主题时有没有踩准具体哪一天要重要得多。我觉得这是很有洞见的一点。选择市场时机非常难，无论你有多少经验都是如此。

turns.en: Natika, stay invested over the long term, seems to be the best thing that you can do. Christie, actually have one more question. This comes from Oscar in New York. How did you enjoy your first appearance on the bid? It was wonderful and painless, I have to say. It's great to see how the magic happens behind the scenes.
turns.zh: Natika，长期保持投资状态（stay invested），似乎就是你能做的最好的事情。Kristy，其实我还有一个问题，这个问题来自纽约的 Oscar：你享受自己在 The Bid 的首次亮相吗？我得说，非常愉快，也毫不痛苦。能看到幕后这套「魔法」是怎么运转的，感觉很棒。

turns.en: While we put you in the hot seat, we threw a lot of random questions at you from our listener base. Thank you for educating us on a wide variety of topics. We look forward to having you back. Thanks for joining us on the bid. Thanks so much for having me. Thanks for listening to this episode of the bid.
turns.zh: 我们把你放到了「热板凳」上，从我们的听众群里抛给你一大堆各种各样的随机问题。感谢你在这么多话题上给我们科普，我们期待你再来做客。感谢你来 The Bid。非常感谢你们的邀请。感谢大家收听本期 The Bid。
